title: INDIA bloc to launch nationwide campaign against CEC, SIR from October 2
author: Sobhana K. Nair
content_html:
The INDIA bloc on Wednesday (September 30, 2026) announced a nationwide campaign beginning Friday (October 2, 2026) with a graded agitation plan that includes protest marches at district headquarters, public meetings, a march to the Election Commission and a joint appeal to the Chief Justice for expedited hearings in cases related to the SIR and alleged electoral “malpractices”.

The decisions were taken after a three-and-a-half-hour meeting attended by 33 leaders from 19 political parties. Independent MP and senior Supreme Court lawyer Kapil Sibal also participated.

Mr. Sibal recommended that the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, should be legally challenged. The legislation states that “notwithstanding other laws, no court could entertain or continue civil or criminal proceedings against a person who was or had been CEC/EC for an act, thing, or word committed, done, or spoken while discharging official duty or function,” extending a blanket immunity to the CEC. In view of this, he suggested that legal action be taken against other Election Commission officials such as Seema Khanna, Director General (IT) at ECI, who have been instrumental in bringing Special Intensive Revision (SIR). Most leaders backed the proposal.

There was, however, apprehension among some leaders about the Supreme Court’s stance. Shiv Sena (UBT) leader and former Maharashtra Chief Minister Uddhav Thackeray, who joined the meeting virtually, cited the Chief Justice of India’s observation while declining an early hearing of pleas related to the SIR in West Bengal. The CJI had observed, “These are only by-elections.”

There was no direct reference to involving the Cockroach Janata Party. However, leaders agreed that the bloc should engage with civil society and secular parties outside the INDIA alliance.

Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the leaders had agreed to fight together. “With unanimity, everyone vowed to fight together,” he said at a press conference attended by top INDIA bloc leaders.

Mr. Kharge alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah were making the Election Commission function like a “puppet”. “These people are only winning elections by stealing votes. When our people oppose this, they are harassed,” he said. He alleged that the BJP was winning elections because they were “stolen”.

Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi alleged that democratic institutions were under attack from the BJP, Mr. Modi, Mr. Shah and CEC Gyanesh Kumar. “We are not going to take it lying down,” he said, adding, “We are going to ensure this personal commitment of all INDIA leaders—people who have destroyed Indian democracy are punished, no matter how senior they are and who they are. Indian democracy is bigger than every single person in this country.”

“Save Democracy” marches

The bloc will hold “Save Democracy” marches in every district between October 2 and 8. The proposal, made by CPI(ML) general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya, initially faced resistance from some leaders citing State-specific political concerns. Senior Congress leaders, including Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi, eventually backed it.

On October 6, Opposition MPs will march to the Election Commission headquarters. Mr. Kharge said some leaders had wanted to hold the march on Wednesday itself, though others suggested a later date to allow all MPs to participate. 

The leaders will also seek an appointment with the President to brief her on the “constitutional hurdles being created by the government”. During the meeting, Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah expressed concern that such requests were often declined or the President’s office limited the size of the delegation. 

The INDIA bloc will also hold five rallies across the country during October and November, including one in Delhi on November 1.

DMK among absentees

Notable absentees included the DMK, which has refused to share a stage with Congress after the latter switched its support to the TVK following the Tamil Nadu Assembly elections. Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav skipped the meeting because of Rajya Sabha polls in his State. JMM chief and Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren joined the meeting virtually.

The parties represented at the meeting included the Congress, Samajwadi Party, Mamata All India Trinamool Congress, NCP (SP), Shiv Sena (UBT), RJD, CPI(M), CPI, National Conference, PDP, JMM, CPI(ML), IUML, KC(M), MDMK, VCK, RSP, KC(J) and AIFB.

title: Army’s ‘Operation Drishti’ in Kashmir’s border areas a milestone: J&K L-G Manoj Sinha
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Jammu and Kashmir (J&K) Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha on Wednesday (September 30, 2026) praised the Army for conducting 144 eye surgeries in Kashmir and termed it “a historic milestone”.

“Despite challenging terrain and the constant threat, doctors and soldiers created an underground operation theatre and restored vision to 220 patients in just two days,” said Mr. Sinha, who spoke at the closing ceremony of Indian Army’s Mega Eye Surgical Camp under ‘Operation Drishti’.

Appreciating the “selfless service” of Brigadier Sanjay Kumar Mishra and his team, Mr. Sinha said the Operation Drishti was a living embodiment of service, compassion, courage, and resolve. 

“144 surgeries were successfully performed at the Srinagar camp, while the Tangdhar camp in Kupwara district marked a historic milestone as the first mega eye surgery camp on the border,” he said.

Mr. Sinha said those who have seen Tangdhar’s geographical conditions understand that reaching there with assistance is itself a challenge. “One must cross mountains, traverse difficult terrain and at times advance even amidst the danger. Yet, in this very challenging and uncertain environment, our doctors and brave soldiers, under the leadership of Brigadier Sanjay Mishra, created a centre of hope,” Mr. Sinha said.

He said modern surgical tools were airlifted to Tangdhar, enabling advanced eye care in a region where such facilities were previously unimaginable. Patients from Khawarpora, Tangdhar, Bagbella, and surrounding villages benefitted from the camp.

“This is true courage, dedication to duty and the real meaning of service. This entire effort has proven one thing beyond doubt that where resolve is firm, no difficulty, however great, can block the path of human service by Indian Army,” the Lieutenant Governor said.

He said more than 1.5 lakh people have undergone eye examinations and more than 3,500 surgeries have been performed across 10 cities under Operation Drishti.

“Indian Army is not only a force that defends the country from external threats, but also a source of support, compassion and healing for ordinary citizens of Jammu Kashmir in times of need. By restoring sight, the Army has given patients a new vision of peace, trust, and togetherness,” he said.

He said the experience of Operation Drishti gives us confidence that with determination, better planning and compassion, modern medicine can be delivered to every corner of the country.

“This is the resolve of “Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas” and under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, it is being ensured that no citizen is left behind,” the Lieutenant Governor said.

title: RSS leader Sunil Ambekar flags demographic changes, calls for scrutiny of population policies
author: Ishita Mishra
content_html:
Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh’s (RSS) national publicity in-charge Sunil Ambekar on Tuesday (September 28, 2026) said that marriage laws framed post-Independence allowed certain communities to have more than one spouse while penalising Hindus from doing so, and that this contributed to demographic disparities.

Speaking at the Indira Gandhi Centre for Arts at the launch of a book titled Secularvaad aur Badalti Jansankhya ke Aankde (Secularism and Changing Population Figures), Mr. Ambekar said that population implications should have been weighed when such laws were framed.

“After 1947, after the Constitution was framed, laws in our country were formulated in such a way that a difference can be seen between the period before and after independence. For example, some people were allowed to have four marriages, whereas Hindus were told that having more than one marriage would be punishable. The law should be the same for everyone. But if a law is created under which one group is legally given an exemption while another is punished for the same conduct, that creates an imbalance,” he said, in his speech in Hindi.

His statement came days after Home Minister Amit Shah had announced that BJP-led NDA will implement Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in 21 States by 2029, ensuring equal rights and justice for all.

According to Mr. Ambekar, the education system created for minorities post Independence had also created imbalance.

“If you go to several States, including Kerala, you will find a large number of minority institutions or educational institutions. As a result, many sections of society have effectively been made to feel that they should go to these particular institutions,” he said, claiming that this had become one route for religious conversions.

He also criticised panchayat rules on family size. “Population control should certainly be considered. But how were these laws introduced? It was said that if you had more than a certain number of children, you could no longer contest a panchayat election,” he said, adding that the rule was not applied equally to all.

He said India lacked a concrete population policy after Independence, and that the first population commission was set up in 2000 under the Vajpayee government.

Backing the National Register of Citizens (NRC) and the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA), the RSS leader said they were needed to identify illegal entrants and grant citizenship to persecuted minorities from neighbouring countries. He said grievances should go through legal channels, but that recognising a non-citizen as a citizen for ‘political reasons’ would be wrong.

“If people have entered the voter list incorrectly, they need to be identified.” he added.

He urged the audience to view the subject of demographic imbalance after “removing the ‘secular’ and ‘communal’ lenses.”

title: Pilot attacked in flydubai altercation Indian
author: Jagriti Chandra
content_html:
The captain who was attacked during an altercation inside the cockpit of a flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv on Wednesday (September 30, 2026) is an Indian national, Captain Smit Machchhar, according to industry sources.

Mr. Machchaar was previously employed with SpiceJet. Official confirmation is awaited.

In a press statement, flydubai has called the incident aboard FZ 1073 “an altercation”.

“At this early stage, the underlying reasons and motives behind this event are unknown and remain subject to a formal investigation,” according to the press statement.

The airline said that the aircraft was successfully secured by on-duty flydubai crew travelling on the flight, who diverted and landed the aircraft safely at Tabuk Airport (TUU) in Saudi Arabia, and that all passengers and crew were safe and accounted for. 

flydubai, in a statement, said that flights to and from Israel will be suspended while the investigation regarding the incident continues.

Pilot Machchaar receiving necessary medical attention: Indian Embassy

The Indian Embassy in Riyadh said that it has been following the health condition of Mr. Machchhar along with the Consulate in Jeddah. “He is admitted in a hospital in Tabuk city in northwest Saudi Arabia and receiving necessary medical attention. A full update on his health is awaited but he is reported to be in stable condition,” the embassy posted on X.

“We hope that he recovers from his injuries at the earliest. We are in touch with his family and assure them that we will continue to follow up on his health with Saudi authorities and extend all possible assistance for his wellbeing.”

title: Modi, Trump review bilateral ties amid concerns over Russia sanctions
author: Suhasini Haidar
content_html:
In their first telephone call since the United States (U.S.) Congress passed the new Russian sanctions law, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said he and President Donald Trump had a “productive conversation” and reviewed bilateral ties.

Mr. Modi and Mr. Trump spoke amid growing concerns over the India-U.S. relationship, underlined by a talk by External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar in New York earlier this week where he spelt out a number of “issues”, including over tariffs, FTA negotiations, the U.S.’s treatment of Indian migrants and Pakistan.

Data Story | 100% U.S. tariff threat: Can India’s new trade deals reduce its dependence on America?

The call between the two leaders followed talks between Mr. Jaishankar and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio as well as Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri and U.S. Undersecretary of State Allison Hooker on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA). During both meetings, Indian officials had raised concerns over the U.S.’s new Lindsey O Graham Sanctions Against Russia and Iran Act (SRIA), which mandates Mr. Trump to levy up to 100% tariffs on goods imported from India, China and other countries that import Russian oil. Mr. Misri also raised the issues with a U.S. Congressional delegation in Delhi this week. 

In a social media post, Mr. Modi said he and Mr. Trump discussed India-U.S. cooperation in “trade, defence, energy, critical technologies and other areas”, but made no direct reference to the SRIA.  

‘Close engagement’

“We agreed to maintain close engagement to take our Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership forward. We also exchanged views on regional and international issues, including ongoing efforts to advance global peace and security,” he said.

On December 14-15, Mr. Modi is expected to travel to Florida to attend the G20 summit hosted by Mr. Trump. Officials said it was too early to confirm whether Mr. Modi, who will travel to Canada prior to that, would also hold bilateral talks with Mr. Trump, and indicated that the progress in the talks for the Free Trade Agreement (FTA), which the U.S. is keen to complete quickly, could determine the engagement. 

Had a productive conversation with President Trump. We reviewed our bilateral cooperation in trade, defence, energy, critical technologies and other areas. We agreed to maintain close engagement to take our Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership forward.

We also exchanged…

— Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) September 30, 2026

At a talk at the Asia Society in New York this week, Mr. Jaishankar acknowledged that New Delhi had several pending issues with the U.S., although he said “much of the world has had a more difficult relationship with the U.S.” as well.

Mr. Jaishankar said the FTA negotiations were “complex” given the 30-fold difference in the per capita income between India and U.S., agricultural needs and production capacity, and the pace of negotiations had created “bumps in the relationship”.

“So the expectation that it could rapidly move forward, was tested against a ground reality which was much more complex,” Mr. Jaishankar said. He said while there was now “more or less” an understanding on the trade agreement, the problems now emanated from the U.S. courts, that struck down Mr. Trump’s “reciprocal tariffs”, and the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR), that has brought in new tariffs according to its “Section 301” investigations. 

Another issue, Mr. Jaishankar said, was the U.S. relationship with Pakistan, despite India’s concerns over cross-border terrorism.

“There are very few countries which have been subjected to the kind of terrorism that we have from a neighbour (Pakistan) as part of a deliberate, conscious policy over many, many decades. Now, if something which matters so deeply to us, [and] there isn’t enough understanding or appreciation or empathy of that, I think that creates a problem,” he said.. 

Mr. Jaishankar said the U.S.’s domestic policies on immigration also had an impact on the relationship due to public opinion in India.  “For many years mobility was seen as an economic gain. Now, today the economics of mobility and the politics of mobility are at odds with each other, at least in some quarters. And that, certainly in public perception [in India] is an issue,” he said, in conversation with Asia Society Distinguished Fellow Daniel Russel on Monday (September 28, 2026).

title: Congress stages protest in Visakhapatnam over SIR exercise
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
The Congress organised a protest at the Gandhi statue near the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) office in Visakhapatnam, opposing what its leaders alleged was the deletion of voters during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process. The protesters demanded that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar be arrested.

Visakhapatnam district Congress president Hasini Varma alleged that the deletion of lakhs of votes in the name of SIR was against democratic principles and demanded action against those responsible. Senior Congress leader Vegi Venkatesh alleged that attempts were being made to delete the votes of Congress sympathisers.

The protesters demanded protection of the right to vote and raised slogans including “Modi Hatao, Desh Bachao” and “Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod”. They later took out a rally from the GVMC office to the Indira Gandhi statue and formed a human chain.

Several Congress leaders and workers participated in the protest.

title: Amazon Now sees strong response in Visakhapatnam
author: Paul Nicodemus
content_html:
Amazon has begun its “Amazon Now” quick-delivery service in Visakhapatnam a few weeks ago, fulfilling orders from nine stores of More Retail Limited in the city.

On Wednesday, Srikant Sree Ram, Director, Everyday Essentials, Amazon India, at an interaction in the city, said the response has been encouraging. “Amazon Now orders are almost 6 to 7 times more than what we used to get in Fresh,” he said, referring to the earlier “Amazon Fresh” service. “Within 4 to 6 weeks, 40% of them are coming back to purchase.”

The service was introduced in India in early 2025. “Amazon Now has crossed $1 billion in annualised gross sales in India, with orders doubling every quarter since launch,” Mr. Sree Ram said, adding that Amazon would reach 100 cities by Diwali. In Andhra Pradesh, it is available in twenty cities, including Guntur, Nellore, Tirupati, Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur, Vijayawada and Rajahmundry, among other places.

On buying patterns, he said, “About 40% of products in every order are non-grocery.” Demand was also shifting towards healthier products. “We see a clear shift of customers looking for clean labels, looking for healthy products,” he said. Sales of dry fruits and nuts were up 60% over normal levels, with almonds nearly tripling. Orders peaked around 9 p.m.

Prime members pay no delivery fee on orders above ₹99, and others above ₹149. “There is no convenience fee that is charged, there is no surge fee that is charged,” Mr. Sree Ram said. “We are working with more than 18,000 farmers across the country,” he said of the fruit and vegetable supply chain, which includes a few collection centres in Andhra Pradesh.

More than 25,000 sellers from Andhra Pradesh sell on Amazon, which has over 20 lakh sellers in India. The “Amazon Great Indian Festival” begins on October 8, with deals open to all customers from the first day. SBI card holders will get a 10% instant discount, and “Amazon Now” will be part of the sale.

title: Bihar Cabinet gives nod to Bihar Green Hydrogen Policy, 2026
author: Amit Bhelari
content_html:
Intended to reduce carbon emissions, the Bihar cabinet on Wednesday (September 30, 2026) gave its nod to the draft “Bihar Green Hydrogen Policy, 2026” to promote renewable energy and reduce dependence on imports of natural gas.

Besides, the move will also attract private investment in the field of green hydrogen, and generating employment opportunities in the state, Cabinet Secretariat Department’s Additional Chief Secretary (ACS) Arvind Kumar Chaudhary told reporters here in a post-Cabinet briefing held at IPRD conference room in Patna.

Stating that similar policies have already been introduced in several other States, Mr. Chuadhary said the central government launched the “National Green Hydrogen Mission” in 2023. Its objective is to achieve the goal of energy independence by 2047 by meeting 50 per cent of India’s electricity demand through renewable energy.

This policy will promote production, consumption, market creation, electrolyser manufacturing, and other components across the value chain of green hydrogen and its derivatives, Mr. Chaudhary said while asserting that the policy, basically, is aimed at “decarbonization” and achieving the goal of net zero. 

A target has been set to produce 0.1 million metric tonnes, or 1,00,000 tonnes of green hydrogen per year by 2031, he added.

The vision is to establish 1 GW of electrolyser capacity and achieve approximately 2.5 GW of renewable energy capacity through green hydrogen and its derivative projects, he said.

The policy also aims to attract investments of approximately ₹16,000 crore and generate around 12,000 direct and indirect jobs, ACS said and added that Bihar Renewable Energy Development Agency (BREDA) has been designated as the nodal agency for implementing the policy.

Reduction of VAT rate on ATF 

The Cabinet also decided to reduce the VAT rate on Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) from one per cent to zero percent at RCS-concessional airports in the State under the Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS).

The VAT rate on ATF used as fuel in aircraft was earlier reduced from 29% to a uniform rate of 4% in June 2025, the press note said.

This decision is expected to increase the number of regional flights and have a positive impact on the State’s economy

Creation of posts for Universities 

The Cabinet also approved the creation of 34 posts of officers and employees for administrative purposes of Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee Artificial Intelligence and Computer Science University, Bhagalpur to enable the effective monitoring and smooth functioning of the University. Similarly, it also approved the creation of 34 posts of officers and employees for administrative functioning of Shaheed Jubba Sahni University of Architecture and Civil Engineering, Muzaffarpur.

It also approved the proposal for the contractual engagement of a total of 35 posts across various categories for the smooth functioning of the Buddha Samyak Darshan Museum-cum-Memorial Stupa, Vaishali, as well as the Directorate of Museums and Government Museums, for a period of 11 months or until regular appointments are made, whichever is earlier. 

Chief Minister Hemophilia Scheme

The Bihar Cabinet also decided to implement the “Mukhya Mantri Hemophilia Yojana [Chief Minister Hemophilia Scheme]” under the Mukhya Mantri Chikitsa Sahayta Kosh (Chief Minister’s Medical Assistance Fund) to provide better treatment for patients suffering from hemophilia in the State.

Mr. Chaudhary, ACS, said that there are 255 patients of Hemophilia across the State. The one vial of drug Emicizumab, used in the treatment, costs ₹39,723 and 78 vials are required to be administered to the patient if his body weight is 30 kg. 

Under this scheme, the drug Emicizumab will be used with the objective of providing better and quality healthcare facilities to hemophilia patients. Its use will help reduce uncontrolled bleeding and the complications associated with it among patients, the press note said.

Nod for water cannons 

The Cabinet also gave administrative approval for the procurement of 30 Water Cannons at a rate of ₹88 lakh per unit, amounting to a total cost of ₹26.40 crore and 86 new Vajra vehicles at a rate of ₹42 lakh per unit, amounting to a total cost of ₹36.12 crore for the purpose of controlling and strengthening law and order in the State.

Thus, a total cost of ₹62.52 crore will be spent on the procurement of the two items of water cannons and Vajra vehicles. 

The procurement of the proposed vehicles will assist in dealing with law-and-order situations, crowd control, riots, and other emergency situations arising during festivals, fairs, election rallies, and the arrival or movement of distinguished and eminent dignitaries in the state.

A total of 30 decisions were taken at today’s Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary.
